'use strict';
/**
 * add-pair — create or repair an account, and keep an access code and its
 * auth password in step.
 *
 *   node tooling/add-pair.js someone@sage.com            # generates a code
 *   node tooling/add-pair.js someone@sage.com 24681000   # or you choose it (8+ digits)
 *   node tooling/add-pair.js someone@sage.com --remove    # take access away
 *   node tooling/add-pair.js --list                      # who has access
 *   node tooling/add-pair.js --selftest                  # offline, no network
 *
 * WHY A COMMAND AND NOT AN ADMIN PAGE
 * Creating the Supabase account and moving its password need the service_role
 * key. Put that in a browser and it is in the page for anyone to read — the
 * service_role bypasses RLS entirely, so leaking it is leaking the table. A
 * command keeps the master key on one machine.
 *
 * WHERE THE PAIRS LIVE (since 2026-10-14)
 * public.quick_signin_accounts, verified through resolve_pair(email, code).
 * The admin edits rows in the comment panel (Reviewer tab -> Access) and those
 * edits apply immediately; nothing in this repo holds a code any more. This
 * tool writes the same row, plus the one thing the panel cannot do: create the
 * auth account or move its password.
 *
 * THE CODE IS THE ACCOUNT PASSWORD
 * Deliberate: the sign-in paths hand the pair straight to signInWithPassword
 * (or signUp on first use), so a separate secret would be a second thing to
 * keep in sync for no gain. resolve_pair verifies the pairing; Supabase
 * verifies the password.
 *
 * THE BOT ID IS WHY THE PASSWORD MOVE EXISTS

13: // the Health-tracker checkout. It also runs here read-only against the same REST
14: // endpoint, which is how it is tested.
15: //
16: //   node tooling/bot-dispatch.js --once      poll once
